I'm not entirely sure on the idea of other players being able to tag others as I can see that getting abused, for example, if a group wants to harass a specific person they could add a whole bunch of horrible tags to them and ruin that person's experience.

On the other hand, I do like the idea of player tags, but maybe it would be better if it was controlled by the user themselves. It's kind of similar to groups in a way, but would be easier to sort through than the hundreds of unrelated groups that pop up in searches.

Like I could set my tags to "furry" "role play" "pokemon mystery dungeon" "sci-fi" "fantasy" and meet a bunch of people interested in the same stuff in worlds that either have similar tags or maybe only let people with at least one of those tags in there. Could also sort groups with those tags as well and make the search results for groups even better.

If VRChat added a public chat option then we could take this a step further by having chat rooms for each of these tags, which could make things even easier.

details:
I see the same post over and over about trying to meet like-minded people in VRChat. I get that VRChat is full of…unique characters but on the surface, for new players, it can often be off-putting. Not shaming, just pointing it out.

I find it difficult trying to get people into this game, they take one look at the stereotypical edge lord and give it a hard pass.

VRChat has so much to offer, it's just a shame people only see the grotesque parts of the community since it's right there on the surface.

VRChat needs to make it easier to find like-minded people, for everyone. 

But I've been thinking of a system that could potentially work. Let's call it "Player Preference Tags" or "PPT"

The proposed system functions as follows:

Players can assign "Player Tags" to individuals they encounter, such as tags like "Chill," "Nice Person," "Noisy," "Racist," and "as well as other tags like "Furry", "Eboy etc."

These tags are not intended as personal attacks but serve as a means of categorization.

No notifications are sent to the tagged individuals; it is simply a user preference.

With this collected information, VRChat can construct an anonymous user profile, potentially aiding in connecting users with like-minded individuals. For instance, if someone is tagged as a "Furry" multiple times, the system may suggest worlds with other furries who share similar tags, facilitating the opportunity to meet people with common interests.

So, you'd search for a world, look at the server list, find the server with "Suggested Server" written on it (this means that this server has the most tags in common with yours) and then simply join it.

To Tag A Player the process involves hovering over a user, selecting their profile, and utilizing the "Set Tags" option. Users can then assign custom tags such as #Mute, #Furry, #Friendly etc, along with a thumbs-up or thumbs-down on each tag to convey their preference, without necessarily providing a negative review.

So if you like furries, you'd tag it #Furry👍 or if you dislike them #Furry👎

Players can even set their own personal tags, but they’re there to save other players time when tagging. (They could also be used for new users for (x) amount of time). If they’re accurate it’ll be very useful to just select them, then set a thumb up or down.

If tags aren’t accurate, then Players can manually tag them, and in time VRChat could suggest more accurate tags.

This way, VRChat gains insights into Players' Preferences, understanding whether users favour or disfavour certain characteristics. This information enables the platform to suggest worlds/servers that align with users' preferences.

I think something like this could categorically change the social element of vrchat entirely, but at the same time, since it's only for "suggested servers", it wouldn't that be invasive either.
title: "Player Preference Tags"
